event.title: Russians Vote in Parliamentary Elections Amid Ongoing War and Limited Opposition
event.canonical_title: Russians Vote in Parliamentary Elections Amid Ongoing War and Limited Opposition
event.summary: Russians are participating in a three-day parliamentary election, the first since the invasion of Ukraine, where only pro-Kremlin parties are on the ballot. The elections are viewed by many as a means for the Kremlin to reinforce its power and legitimacy, with fears of mobilization overshadowing the voting process. Most anti-war candidates have been excluded, raising concerns about the authenticity of the electoral process.

timeline.title: Voting Begins in Russia's Duma Elections Amid Ongoing Ukraine Conflict
timeline.summary: Voting for Russia's parliamentary elections has commenced, starting in the Far East on September 18 and continuing for three days. Polls will close on Sunday evening, with voters selecting all 450 members of the State Duma. The elections are taking place against the backdrop of the ongoing war in Ukraine.
key_facts: Voting began on September 18, 2026, in the Far East.
The elections will last for three days.
All 450 members of the State Duma will be elected.

timeline.title: Russia Conducts Parliamentary Elections Including Occupied Ukrainian Regions
timeline.summary: Russia is holding parliamentary elections for the first time in regions of Ukraine that it annexed during the ongoing conflict. The elections will fill 450 seats in the State Duma and 11 regional governorships, with only pro-Putin parties on the ballot. The vote is overshadowed by fears of mobilization and is characterized by a lack of genuine opposition.

event_overview.title: About Russia Elections
event_overview.subject: Russia Elections
event_overview.summary: Russia’s 2026 parliamentary election chooses the ninth convocation of the State Duma, the elected lower chamber of the Federal Assembly. Voting is being held during Russia’s war against Ukraine and alongside regional and municipal elections; the political environment has been marked by restrictions on opposition activity.

facts.label: Voting period
facts.value: Voting for the 2026 State Duma election is scheduled across three days, September 18–20, 2026; September 20 is the single voting day.

facts.label: Institution being elected
facts.value: The State Duma is the lower chamber of Russia’s Federal Assembly (parliament) and has 450 deputies.

facts.label: Electoral system
facts.value: The election uses a mixed system: 225 deputies are elected in single-member districts and 225 from federal party lists in proportional representation.

facts.label: Term and election authority
facts.value: State Duma deputies serve five-year terms. Under the federal election law, the president calls regular Duma elections, while election commissions administer the process under election legislation.

facts.label: Voter and candidate eligibility
facts.value: Russian citizens aged 18 or older may vote; a candidate for the State Duma must be at least 21 and permanently reside in Russia, subject to other legal qualifications and restrictions.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline covers the opening of voting on September 18, 2026, rather than the full campaign, regional contests, vote count, certification, or longer-term political consequences.
